title: Token sparkline breakdown — prototype notes
body:
Purpose
This is an exploratory doc for a compact per-token latency + cost visualization that fits into the invocation timeline card (compact mode). Goal: give engineers an immediate signal of where token cost/latency spikes occurred without overwhelming the console with full waterfall charts.

High-level idea
- Show a tiny sparkline per token representing relative latency contribution across the response (micro-sparkline: 16–32px tall).
- Color-code by cost intensity (cool -> warm) and stroke thickness for token length/byte cost.
- Allow quick drilldown: hover shows token text, raw ms, token charge, upstream model variant; click expands a waterfall (same data as existing token-autopsy but scoped to invocation).
- Provide two density modes: Compact (sparklines inline) and Expanded (vertical stacking + token-level histograms).

Why different from existing token views
- Existing token breakdowns are heavyweight and consume vertical space. This is designed for scan-and-find: identify hot tokens in a list of invocations, then jump to deep-dive only when needed.
- Optimized for lists (top N recent invocations) and for long-running streaming sessions where full waterfalls are noisy.

Mock layout (wireframe notes)
- Invocation list row: left = invocation metadata (id, model, duration); middle = micro-sparkline band (scrollable, clipped to 600px); right = cost badge + tiny histogram of token charges.
- Micro-sparkline band specifics: each token = vertical bar; height = normalized latency contribution; color = cost quantile; subtle gap between bars to indicate token boundaries; hover displays tooltip anchored to bar.
- Expanded drill: modal anchored to row with: full waterfall, token list with text, key/value pair (ms, cost, kv-cache reuse flag, attention-skip index).

Interaction patterns
- Hover (fast peek): tooltip with token text (truncate long tokens), ms, cost cents, model variant. Tooltip includes link to invocation trace.
- Click (drill): expand to full waterfall modal. Modal allows keyboard nav: left/right to move tokens, up/down to switch allocation buckets (compute/IO/queue).
- Pin: middle-click or cmd+click pins the waterfall to the right-hand inspector pane for cross-invocation comparisons. Pins persist per user session.
- Streaming: for in-progress invocations, sparklines animate with new bars appended; provide a low-bandwidth mode (sample every N tokens) when network constrained.

Backend considerations / API surface
- API should support returning a small pre-aggregated micro-timeline: {tokens: [{latency_ms_bucket, cost_bucket, token_text_snippet}], summary: {total_ms, total_cost}}. We intentionally avoid sending full per-token ms floats for compact mode.
- Two endpoints: compact-timeline (pre-aggregated, lossy quantization) and full-token-autopsy (raw floats + debug traces). Compact-timeline must be cheap to compute and cacheable.
- Telemetry events: token_sparkline_hover, token_sparkline_click, token_sparkline_pin, compact_timeline_fetch. Include invocation_id and model_variant in payload.

Accessibility & performance notes
- Sparklines must have high-contrast color palette for colorblind users; use patterned fill option for accessibility test. Provide alt-text on expand for screen readers summarizing "peak token at position X contributed Y ms and Z cost".
- Render sparklines using canvas or small SVG groups (avoid heavy DOM for per-token bars). Virtualize when >200 tokens in an invocation.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Compact timeline visible in invocation list for recent invocations -> QA shows correct relative peaks in 90% of sampled calls.
- Hover tooltip shows token snippet, ms quantile, cost cents, link to trace.
- Drill modal opens and matches fields from full token-autopsy (sanity check against raw).
- Backend compact-timeline endpoint returns payload under 8KB for typical 1024-token invocations.

Hypotheses to validate in experiments
- H1: Engineers can identify the offending token (hotspot) faster with sparklines than with top-level duration numbers (target: 20% reduction in mean time to detect in usability test).
- H2: Compact-mode reduces console noise and decreases clicks to open full autopsy by 30%.

Open questions & trade-offs
- Quantization strategy: linear buckets vs log buckets. Recommendation: log buckets for tail-heavy latency distributions (we will A/B).
- Privacy: do we send raw token text in compact mode? Risk vs usefulness. Proposal: send first 16 chars + redaction flag; full token only via full-token-autopsy which requires additional permission.
- Sampling policy for streaming: drop every Nth token vs windowed sampling. Test both on synthetic workloads.

Grooming backlog (actionable items)
- RDW-4023: Backend: implement compact-timeline endpoint with 8KB budget (owner: Marcus)
- RDW-4031: UX: render micro-sparkline component library + accessibility variants (owner: Avery)
- RDW-4034: SRE: stress test virtualization rendering on ~4k token responses (owner: Jonah)
- RDW-4039: Product: define retention policy for compact payloads and PII redaction (owner: Sofia)

Next steps before next sync (09/17)
- Marcus to share draft API spec and sample payloads.
- Avery to produce two visual prototypes (canvas vs SVG) and a short Loom explaining interactions.
- Jonah to run perf baseline for rendering 1k tokens at 60fps (proof-of-concept).
- Sofia to draft short privacy note for Legal review (redaction options).

Notes from last grooming meeting (9/5)
- PM concerns: don't introduce new heavy realtime endpoints without caching. We agreed compact endpoint should be cacheable per-invocation and invalidated on model variant switch.
- UX concern: ensure sparklines don't make rows jump height — cap to fixed band and use overflow with hover-to-scroll.
- Engineering: prefer quantized integer buckets to avoid float bloat across the wire.

Rough sketches (descriptive)
- Card row: [ID | model | 1-line prompt snippet] [micro-sparkline band (600px)] [cost badge] [expand chevron]
- Modal: left = waterfall timeline (full width), right = token list table (token | ms | cost | kv_cache_hit) with keyboard focus and copy token.

If helpful I can produce a rapid sketch PNG in Figma and link it; or create a Loom recording of the proposed interactions.
